native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/python/reference_evaluator_test.py -k "scatter_elements or scatter_mean or scatter_none_string" -q --tb=line
why: Reference ScatterElements walks every index with np.ndindex and writes one element from Python. The workload is a (32, 64, 64) float32 feature-volume update along axis 1, with one permutation of that axis so every index is unique. One along-axis write does the same stores and should remove most of the 49.6 ms. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 calls after one warmup, with gc.collect before each call. Open issue #3234 asks the spec whether duplicate indices are allowed; no open PR edits this function, and this workload does not use duplicates. Dropped col2im (already landed in #8736), GridSample (#8552), add_prefix (#8503, #8756), and external-data save (#8055) because those already have open or merged work.

Reference GatherND appends one Python value per index, then copies the list into an array. The workload gathers 50,000 points from a (96, 64, 48) float32 volume, each index a full coordinate. One advanced-index gather returns the same values and removes the interpreter loop, which is the call. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 calls after one warmup, with gc.collect before each call. No open PR edits _gather_nd_impl. PR #8686 only adds Attention examples that call GatherND; it does not change this function.

Reference NonMaxSuppression builds a Python BoxInfo per box that passes the score threshold, for every class, then sorts those objects and walks them. The workload is one image, 80 classes, and 300 corner-encoded boxes (score 0.5, IoU 0.5, at most 20 kept per class), which is a detector head. Filtering and ordering with arrays, using the same score-then-higher-index order as BoxInfo.__lt__, keeps the selected indices and drops the object traffic. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 calls after one warmup, with gc.collect before each call. No open PR edits this implementation. Issues #2212 and #2360 are closed.
